issues.legal_issue: A lessor may fix a locality-wide market value for calculating unearned increase, and a rate so fixed binds the lessor when it later considers a transfer.
material_facts: The sublease allowed the lessor to recover part of the unearned increase on a transfer and made the lessor’s determination of market value final and binding.
The lessor’s market-value-setting power had been delegated to the relevant government authority.
The lessor and the government authority issued and applied locality-wide market rates for calculating unearned increase, and the government extended the existing rates without increasing them.
issues.conclusion: The circulars fixing locality-wide market rates were valid, and the lessor could not later disregard those rates and determine a different market value for an individual transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 22(3) and 56 of the Delhi Development Act and Rule 23 of the applicable Nazul Land Rules, the sublease could contain terms consistent with its prescribed form. Clause 6(b) of the sublease empowered the lessor to determine market value and made that determination final and binding. Fixing a market value locality-wide was permissible and did not conflict with the Act or Rules. Executive instructions may fill gaps where rules are silent, but may not contradict statutory rules: Sant Ram Sharma v. State of Rajasthan and State of M.P. v. G.S. Dall & Four Mills. Once the lessor fixed and applied a locality-wide rate, it could not resile from that rate in an individual case.

predicates.lease_transfer_permission_case: The proceeding concerns permission to transfer property held under a lease or sublease.
predicates.lease_contains_final_market_value_clause: The lease or sublease gives the lessor authority to determine market value and makes that determination final and binding.
predicates.lessor_fixed_locality_market_rate: The lessor or an authorized government authority fixed a market rate for a locality for calculating the amount recoverable on transfer.

issues.definition: When a transfer-permission proceeding concerns a lease with a final market-value clause and the lessor has fixed a locality-wide rate, that rate binds the lessor.

issues.legal_issue: An unearned-increase demand must be calculated using the applicable market-rate circulars and must account for documented transaction consideration rather than an assumed higher price.
material_facts: A sublessee sought permission to sell the property and disclosed the consideration in the sale agreement and in a tax clearance certificate.
The purchaser agreed to bear part of the unearned increase, but the lessor treated that agreement as establishing a higher hypothetical total transaction value.
The lessor’s demand disregarded the locality rates then in force, which had been extended without an increase.
The lessor did not calculate the demand by applying the circular rates and accounting for the consideration shown in the transaction documents.
issues.conclusion: The demand could not stand as calculated; the unearned increase had to be recalculated under the applicable circular rates, taking account of the consideration stated in the sale agreement or tax clearance certificate.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause 6(b) of the sublease, the lessor could recover a portion of unearned increase, but its determination had to follow the market value it had fixed and made applicable. A demand could not rest on a hypothetical assumption that a purchaser would pay an additional amount, and the lessor was required to take account of the consideration shown in the sale agreement and/or tax clearance certificate. The locality rates fixed by circulars formed part of the applicable lease terms.

rule.if: lease_transfer_permission_case and applicable_locality_rates_were_in_force and demand_used_hypothetical_consideration and transaction_consideration_was_documented

predicates.lease_transfer_permission_case: The proceeding concerns a demand for an amount payable as a condition of permission to transfer leased property.
predicates.applicable_locality_rates_were_in_force: A market rate fixed for the locality was applicable when the transfer demand was made.
predicates.demand_used_hypothetical_consideration: The lessor calculated the demand using an assumed transaction value rather than the applicable locality rate and the disclosed transaction terms.
predicates.transaction_consideration_was_documented: The consideration for the transaction was stated in documents submitted to or available to the lessor.

issues.definition: When a transfer demand uses an assumed value despite applicable locality rates and documented transaction consideration, it must be recalculated using those rates and documents.

issues.legal_issue: A prospective conversion policy does not entitle parties in a pending challenge to an earlier transfer demand to new relief based on a later cause of action when their transfer was completed under an interim order.
material_facts: The challenged demand concerned a transfer and was the subject of pending proceedings.
A later policy provided for conversion of leasehold property to freehold and stated that it operated prospectively and would not reopen cases already decided.
The respondents paid amounts demanded under an interim court order and completed their sale transactions.
A similarly situated applicant who had not paid the demand later obtained the benefit of the conversion policy.
The respondents sought to rely on that later policy in the appeals but had not amended their original proceedings to claim relief based on it.
issues.conclusion: The interim order did not entitle the respondents to the benefit of the later conversion policy, and that policy could not be used in the appeals to substitute a new relief based on a fresh cause of action.
issues.legal_principle: A court may consider subsequent events and mould relief, but may not thereby substitute a new relief founded on a fresh cause of action. A later policy expressly given prospective effect does not apply to an earlier completed transaction merely because another person later obtained its benefit. The Court also noted that the parties could have declined to pay under the interim order and that the later policy had not been contemplated when they proceeded with the transactions.

rule.if: appeal_against_transfer_demand and later_policy_is_prospective and transfer_was_completed_under_interim_order and no_amendment_claimed_new_policy_relief

predicates.appeal_against_transfer_demand: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a demand made as a condition of transferring leased property.
predicates.later_policy_is_prospective: A policy introduced after the challenged demand expressly operates prospectively and does not reopen completed cases.
predicates.transfer_was_completed_under_interim_ord: The affected party paid pursuant to an interim court order and completed the transfer while the challenge was pending.
predicates.no_amendment_claimed_new_policy_relief: The affected party relied on the later policy without amending the original proceeding to claim relief based on a new cause of action.

issues.definition: In an appeal against a transfer demand, a prospective later policy does not provide new relief when the transfer was completed under an interim order and the proceeding was not amended to claim that relief.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may decline to entertain new grounds that a party failed to raise despite repeated opportunities to disclose its position in the proceedings below.
material_facts: The authority had repeated opportunities in the High Court to disclose the policies governing its demands and to clarify its position.
The authority did not adequately comply with those directions and did not distinguish the examples relied on by the High Court.
It sought to distinguish those examples and raise related grounds for the first time on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The authority should not be given an opportunity to raise those new grounds on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A party that failed to disclose its policy or raise relevant distinctions despite repeated opportunities in the court below should not be permitted to introduce those grounds for the first time on appeal. The Court relied on the procedural history of the case and the authority’s failure to comply with the High Court’s opportunities and directions.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and party_had_repeated_opportunities_below and party_failed_to_disclose_relevant_position and new_ground_raised_first_on_appeal

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision made after litigation in a lower court.
predicates.party_had_repeated_opportunities_below: The party received repeated opportunities in the lower court to state its position or provide relevant information.
predicates.party_failed_to_disclose_relevant_positi: The party did not adequately disclose its relevant policy or factual position despite those opportunities.
predicates.new_ground_raised_first_on_appeal: The party sought to rely on a ground or distinction that it had not raised in the lower court.

issues.definition: When a party repeatedly had an opportunity to disclose its position below but raises a new ground only on appeal, the appellate court may decline to consider it.

issues.legal_issue: A court may reduce a previously ordered interest rate when the rate is discretionary and changed commercial conditions make the original rate excessive, while preserving a higher rate for failure to pay within the time directed.
material_facts: The High Court’s interim order provided for interest at 18% on any amount to be refunded.
The litigation had continued for a substantial period, and commercial and bank interest rates had fallen substantially.

The Supreme Court considered restitution and concluded that a lower rate would meet the ends of justice, while directing payment within six weeks and providing for the higher rate if payment was not made in that time.
issues.conclusion: The interest rate was reduced to 9% per annum, with the original 18% rate applying after the six-week payment period if the amount remained unpaid.
issues.legal_principle: Interest pendente lite and future interest are discretionary, and an appellate court may exercise the same power as the court below, guided by the principle in Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the need for restitution. Interest in equity depends on the circumstances: South Eastern Coalfields Ltd. v. State of M.P. The Court also relied on K.T. Venkatagiri v. State of Karnataka and Pure Helium India Pvt. Ltd. v. Oil & Natural Gas Commission in considering an appropriate rate, and on the principle that changed commercial rates may justify reducing an earlier rate.

predicates.appeal_concerning_interest_on_refundable: The proceeding concerns interest payable on an amount to be refunded or repaid.
predicates.interest_is_discretionary: The court has discretion to determine the applicable interest rate.
predicates.prevailing_commercial_rates_have_fallen: Commercial or bank interest rates have substantially declined since the earlier interest rate was ordered.
predicates.payment_is_directed_within_a_specified_t: The court directs payment by a deadline and makes the interest consequence depend on compliance with it.

issues.definition: When interest is discretionary, prevailing commercial rates have fallen, and payment is ordered by a deadline, the court may set a reduced rate and make a higher rate apply if payment is late.
